title: PERSCEN: Learning Personalized Interaction Pattern and Scenario Preference for Multi-Scenario Matching

problem.claim: Multi-scenario recommendation needs to model both preferences shared across scenarios and preferences specific to each scenario.

gap.claim: Existing methods often overlook user-specific modeling, limiting personalized user representations.

contributions.claim: PERSCEN incorporates user-specific modeling into multi-scenario matching.
PERSCEN constructs a user-specific feature graph and applies a lightweight graph neural network to capture higher-order interaction patterns and extract shared preferences.
PERSCEN uses vector quantization to distill scenario-aware preferences from within-scenario behavior sequences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show PERSCEN outperforming existing methods.
The authors report that efficiency analysis shows PERSCEN balances performance with computational cost for practical industrial use.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-scenario matching is presented as a mainstream response to expanding online-platform business scales and scopes.
Effective recommendation requires shared and scenario-specific user preferences.
Existing methods insufficiently model user-specific representations.
PERSCEN combines user-specific graph modeling, vector-quantized scenario preference distillation, and gated fusion.
The authors report improved performance and a favorable performance–computational-cost balance.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, metric values, baselines, or experimental conditions.
